items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I learned that she had been among the young girls that went to the house on Hathaway Street when Dolly and Dyer Jones went there to rehearse

ctx.x: We lived on the 5th Street between Mound and Cutter Street over an undertaker parlor. The name of the undertaker was Mr. Copeland. When we lived on Barr Street, the Coplands lived across the street from me and I used to make candy-spending money from Mrs. Copland by watering her lawn in the summer and shoveling coal into her cellar in the winter.

Dolly Jones left Cincinnati along with her mother who's name was Dyer Jones. Some medicine shows came to town and they used to put on their show in any empty lot they could find and no one had to pay to see them. The supposed doctor sold bottles of syrup that was supposed to be good for the liver, rheumatism, heart trouble, and pills for blood circulation, aching bones or any kind of sickness that existed. Medicine to cure all ailments.

There were always some kind of musicians playing those shows and a couple of comedians. Some of the jokes were: How do you feel, Mr. Bones? and Mr. Bones would answer: Just like a stove! The other one would ask: How's that? and Mr. Bones would answer: Red hot and still a heating.
